Thanks,
Sarah

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal: order form + term ask

Hi Sarah — thanks for the order form. We reviewed internally and attached a tracked-change redline for the MSA and a PDF callout for the order form. High-level notes below (see redline for clause-level edits):

1) Term: Redwood is fine with an 18-month fixed term, subject to section 5 auto-renewal language being updated (we propose auto-renew by mutual written agreement rather than unilateral renewal).
2) Indemnity / liability cap: CloudBridge requested a broader indemnity carveout for third-party IP claims. We propose a mutual IP defense clause plus a liability cap equal to 12 months of fees (we are willing to discuss movement but need a reciprocal standard).
3) SLA credits: We can accommodate an SLA schedule addendum; credit calculation will be capped and applied per monthly invoice — please confirm whether CloudBridge expects service credits or a fee rebate.
4) Data retention & audit: Added explicit language for audit access and data deletion timelines for PII; if CloudBridge requires a SOC 2 report handoff, please confirm the contact.
5) Order form scope: Clarified burst billing (per-token overage at the published overage rate) and added an Exhibit for seat-tier mappings.

Attached: [MSA_Redline_v3.docx (tracked changes)], [OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf (PDF with callouts)]

Requested next steps:
- Sarah: confirm whether the indemnity cap or mutual defense approach is a blocker.
- Priyom/Ben: confirm final numbers for committed 7M tokens and proposed overage pricing for +50% burst so Marissa can sanity-check the fee cap language.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@cloudbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: order form + term ask

Marissa — appreciate the quick pass and the clear notes. A couple quick responses:

- Indemnity: Procurement prefers a mutual defense + a mutual cap tied to 12 months of fees; however, legal is pushing for excluding direct product liability for certain agent integrations. Can we add a narrowly tailored carveout rather than a broad exclusion?
- SLA credits: Would prefer fee rebates over service credits (they’re easier for our finance team to apply).
- SOC 2: Yes — we’ll accept Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report. I’ll send the contact after this thread (our security team is cc’d in a separate ticket).
- Burst billing: procurement asked if you can discount the overage rate for the first two months of the ramp to 75% of published overage to help with onboarding spikes.

Attaching: [CloudBridge_PO_20270415.pdf (PO stub)]

If we can align on indemnity language + a short onboarding discount for burst, procurement can sign-off and we’ll route to DocuSign.

Best,
Sarah
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@cloudbridge.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: order form + term ask

Sarah — thanks. Quick pricing math and a proposed path:

- Committed: 7,000,000 tokens/mo at $0.0009/token = $6,300/mo (committed rate).
- Burst overage: published rate $0.0014/token; we can offer onboarding discount of 25% off published overage for the first two invoice cycles on actual overage consumption (i.e., charge at $0.00105/token for first two months).
- Liability cap proposal: mutual cap = 12 months of committed fees (proposed cap = $75,600), with a narrowly tailored carveout for gross negligence and IP indemnity preserved. Marissa — please confirm this aligns with the redline.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to incorporate the mutual cap language + carveout as discussed into MSA_Redline_v4.
2) Priyom to update the order form with the 7M committed line, burst description, and the two-month onboarding discount clause.
3) Once redlines are accepted by CloudBridge, Priyom will open the DocuSign envelope (link below) and procurement will route the PO.
